title: Economic Update Q2 2026
summary: Explore the state of the economy in Q2 2026 as growth rebounded on stronger consumer spending and technology investment. This analysis covers improving housing activity, resilient CRE fundamentals, and AI-driven data center growth amid inflation pressures and elevated rates.
body_text: The economy rebounded during the second quarter, bolstered by larger consumer tax refunds and continued business investment in technology. However, the Iran conflict introduced new uncertainty, triggered an oil price shock, and renewed inflationary pressures. As a result, the benchmark 10-year Treasury yield rose to its highest level in more than a year during May. Against this backdrop, the Federal Reserve (the Fed) maintained its focus on inflation and left policy rates unchanged. Residential Real Estate Economic uncertainty contributed to a measured pace of activity in the residential housing market this spring. Improved affordability encouraged purchases during the quarter, as reflected by Existing and New sales that improved 2.0% and 5.3% over Q1, respectively. Builders facing elevated inventory levels raised their price concessions 1 and sale incentives, while many existing homeowners reduced asking prices 2 to attract buyers. The importance of location may have become even more pronounced, as illustrated in the latest FHFA House Price Index Quarterly Report . Beyond pricing, buyers and sellers appeared increasingly willing to adapt to a market characterized by elevated interest rates and economic uncertainty. As Realtor.com noted, participants are developing a more “recalibrated attitude” toward these conditions. This change was evident in new listings in May that reached their highest level in four years, in addition to the jump in first-time home buyers 3 willing to come off the sidelines. However, improving activity was constrained by weaker buyer confidence and the highest 30-year fixed mortgage interest rates in nine months. Builders also scaled back housing starts as they worked through elevated inventory levels and rising material costs. Commercial Real Estate The CRE market remained resilient during the second quarter, despite encountering several new headwinds. Investors and lenders remained active but cautious as they assessed the inflationary implications of the conflict in Iran and the mid-May surge in the benchmark 10-year treasury4 yield . Transaction volume across the four major property sectors is projected to reach approximately $74 billion, slightly below last quarter, according to an analysis of CoStar data. Even so, annual growth remained in the double digits, while property prices continued to rise. Delinquencies edged higher in Q1 but remained uneven across property types and had limited impact on distressed transaction activity. Retail cap rates increased modestly, largely due to movement in the mall segment. Property fundamentals continued to normalize across major asset classes, per CoStar. Office performance improved gradually, while limited new supply supported Retail occupancy. Multifamily fundamentals strengthened as construction starts fell to a decade low. Industrial continued to work through speculative inventory, with vacancy and rent growth returning to more typical levels. Despite transportation-related disruptions from the conflict in Iran, technology-driven manufacturing supported demand and absorption. With the explosion of the Artificial Intelligence (AI) industry, data centers were a big driver of business investment, added construction employment, and supported the industrial manufacturing resurgence. Their inventory 5 spans almost every region of the country. And although data center property and land sales were not a big portion of the overall CRE transaction pie, their growth was exceptionally strong. In 2025, data center land transactions increased five-fold, while existing data centers’ sale volume rose 36%. Transaction activity through June for both types of sales was ahead of last year’s pace. Much of this activity was driven by the substantial expansion plans among major technology companies. However, the trajectory of future data center development is less clear. Although the federal government 6 offers federal land for data centers, more states and localities 7 are curbing or halting further expansion. Employment should be solid, although consumers face a fall in real wages while business investment normalizes. The MBA expects the oil price shock of the last few months to wind its way through inflation this summer, bringing no relief to the Treasury yield or mortgage rates. Although the Fed Funds rate was kept the same in Q2, Board members became more divided on the appropriate future path. Despite the new Fed Chair’s clear and often-stated commitment to the Fed’s 2% inflation target, no movement in the Fed Funds rate is expected at their July meeting (or even this year). Median prices are expected to decrease and the FHFA House Price Index could drop below 1.0% for the first time in 14 years. CRE transaction activity is expected to remain stable as property fundamentals continue to normalize. Indeed, if buyers and sellers are increasingly willing to bring prices together as recently reported 8, it could provide additional momentum for transaction growth. title: First Principles of Engineering Metrics
summary: Discover how software engineering metrics empower teams to improve delivery speed, quality, & predictability. Learn actionable strategies to track agile development metrics, enhance software quality metrics, & align engineering efforts with business goals. Developer productivity metrics by Haystack.
body_text: In software engineering, success isn’t just about building innovative products—it’s also about ensuring that the process of creation is efficient, predictable, and aligned with business goals. How do you measure whether your engineering efforts are moving in the right direction? The answer lies in engineering metrics. These metrics go beyond vanity numbers or arbitrary benchmarks. They offer a window into the health and efficiency of your engineering processes, empowering teams to identify bottlenecks, prioritize improvements, and ultimately deliver more value to users and stakeholders. In this blog, we’ll explore the first principles of engineering metrics —what they are, why they matter, and how you can implement them to transform your team’s performance. Why Metrics Matter for Engineering Teams Engineering teams are the backbone of product innovation, yet their impact is often underrepresented. Unlike sales or marketing, which have clear revenue and lead metrics, engineering operates in a realm where outcomes are less tangible. This lack of visibility can lead to: Misalignment with Business Goals : Without measurable outcomes, engineering teams may pursue goals that don’t align with organizational priorities. Inefficiencies : Teams might focus on the wrong areas, leading to wasted time and resources. Inconsistent Delivery : Without metrics, it’s challenging to ensure predictable and high-quality delivery . By adopting engineering metrics, teams can quantify their progress, communicate effectively with stakeholders, and demonstrate their value to the organization. What Are Engineering Metrics? At their core, engineering metrics are quantitative measurements that provide insights into the productivity, quality, and efficiency of software development. These metrics help teams track progress, identify issues, and align efforts with broader organizational goals. Key attributes of effective engineering metrics include: Actionability : Metrics should inform decision-making. Relevance : Focus on what impacts your team’s success. ‍ Transparency : Stakeholders should easily understand the metrics. By implementing the right metrics, engineering teams can shift from reactive problem-solving to proactive optimization. A First-Principles Approach to Metrics The first-principles approach simplifies metrics by focusing on the foundational responsibilities of any engineering team. By asking, what would cause the team to fail? , we uncover critical areas for measurement: Speed : Can the team deliver quickly enough to meet business demands? Quality : Does the team deliver code that works as expected? Predictability : Can the team deliver consistently and on schedule? Each of these pillars requires targeted metrics to monitor and improve performance. Key Metrics for Engineering Teams 1. Speed Metrics Speed is essential for maintaining a competitive edge. The faster a team delivers value, the sooner stakeholders see results. Core Speed Metrics : Cycle Time : Measures the duration between starting and completing a task. Lead Time : Tracks how long it takes for a request to move from initiation to delivery. Deployment Frequency : Reflects how often new code is deployed to production. Strategies to Improve Speed : Automate repetitive processes such as testing and deployments. Break down large projects into smaller, manageable tasks. Use tools like Haystack to identify bottlenecks in workflows. 2. Quality Metrics Quality ensures that delivered products meet user expectations and are free of defects. Poor quality can lead to customer dissatisfaction, increased costs, and a damaged reputation. Core Quality Metrics : Defect Density : Measures the number of defects relative to code volume. Escaped Defects : Counts bugs that reach production. Code Churn : Tracks the frequency of code changes after initial delivery. Improving Quality : Implement rigorous code reviews and testing processes. Encourage knowledge sharing to standardize coding practices. Regularly monitor user feedback to identify areas for improvement. 3. Predictability Metrics Predictability is critical for aligning engineering efforts with business objectives. Teams that deliver reliably build trust with stakeholders. Core Predictability Metrics : Sprint Velocity : The amount of work completed in a sprint. Commit-to-Deploy Ratio : Reflects the efficiency of the development pipeline. On-Time Delivery Rate : Measures the percentage of tasks completed on schedule. Improving Predictability : Use historical data to set realistic timelines. Reduce work-in-progress (WIP) to maintain focus. Adopt agile practices like daily standups and retrospective meetings. Common Pitfalls in Engineering Metrics Tracking metrics is valuable, but misusing them can do more harm than good. Some common pitfalls include: Focusing on Vanity Metrics : Metrics like "lines of code written" provide no actionable insights. Gaming Metrics : Teams may prioritize meeting a metric at the expense of actual outcomes. Tracking Too Many Metrics : Overloading teams with metrics can dilute focus. How to Avoid Pitfalls : Prioritize metrics that align with business goals. Regularly review metrics to ensure they remain relevant. Involve team members in choosing and interpreting metrics. Aligning Metrics with Business Objectives The ultimate goal of metrics is to bridge the gap between engineering efforts and business outcomes. Here’s a quick comparison of department-specific metrics and their purposes: Department Core Metric Purpose Sales Revenue Tracks income generated by closing deals. Marketing Marketing Qualified Leads (MQLs) Measures the quality of leads generated. Engineering Speed, Quality, Predictability Demonstrates process efficiency and output value. ‍ By aligning metrics with business objectives, engineering teams can showcase their impact in terms that resonate with stakeholders. Advanced Metrics for Mature Teams Once the basics are in place, advanced metrics can provide deeper insights: Customer Impact Metrics : Tracks how engineering output influences user satisfaction. Team Health Metrics : Monitors factors like developer burnout and collaboration efficiency. ‍ DORA Metrics : Deployment frequency, lead time for changes, mean time to recovery (MTTR), and change failure rate. How Haystack Simplifies Metrics Tracking Tracking metrics manually can be time-consuming and error-prone. Haystack’s platform streamlines the process by providing real-time insights into: Workflow Efficiency : Identify bottlenecks in the development process. Delivery Speed : Monitor deployment frequency and lead time. Code Quality : Track defect rates and code churn. With Haystack , engineering teams can focus on what matters—delivering value—without the overhead of manual reporting. Conclusion Metrics are the cornerstone of a mature engineering organization. By focusing on speed, quality, and predictability, teams can enhance their performance and deliver tangible business value. The first-principles approach simplifies the process of choosing metrics, ensuring they remain relevant and actionable. Whether you’re a CTO, Engineering Manager, or team lead, investing time in defining and tracking the right metrics will pay dividends in the form of improved productivity, higher-quality deliverables, and stronger alignment with business goals.

title: Xcel Energy Completes Sherco Solar Phase 3
summary: CLEAR LAKE, Minn., (July 21, 2026) — Xcel Energy announced the completion of Sherco Solar Phase 3, marking another major milestone in the company's transformation of a retiring coal plant into a major renewable energy hub. Located near the existing ...
body_text: CLEAR LAKE, Minn., (July 21, 2026) — Xcel Energy announced the completion of Sherco Solar Phase 3, marking another major milestone in the company's transformation of a retiring coal plant into a major renewable energy hub. Located near the existing Sherco plant in Becker, Sherco Solar is the largest solar facility in Minnesota and one of the biggest in the Upper Midwest. With the first three phases online, the site now produces 710 megawatts of electricity powered by 1.7 million solar panels. A proposed fourth phase would bring the Sherco Solar’s total generating capacity to 910 megawatts – capable of powering more than 190,000 homes – by 2029. The expansion will create an estimated 300 union construction jobs and $90 million in local economic benefits. "Completing Sherco Solar Phase 3 is a significant step in our efforts to deliver the reliable, affordable and increasingly clean energy our customers expect," said Bria Shea, president of Xcel Energy–Minnesota, North Dakota and South Dakota. "This project demonstrates how we can build upon existing infrastructure and workforce expertise to meet growing energy needs, create economic opportunities for Minnesota communities and continue advancing our renewable energy transition." "As someone who grew up in this community and works at this site, it's exciting to see the next chapter of Sherco taking shape," said Luke Molus, senior operations manager for Xcel Energy's solar and storage sites. "For decades, the Sherco plant has helped power our region, and today Sherco Solar is continuing that legacy by delivering reliable energy for customers and creating a new future for this site and the people who work here." Sherco Solar is a key component of Xcel Energy's strategy to maintain reliability while expanding renewable energy resources and keeping customer bills as low as possible. The project also reinforces Becker's longstanding role as an energy-producing community and highlights how existing power plant sites can support the next generation of energy infrastructure. # # # About Xcel Energy Xcel Energy (NASDAQ: XEL) is a leading energy provider, dedicated to serving millions of customers with excellence. We make energy work better for customers, helping them thrive every day. That means always raising the bar — delivering better service and providing more reliable, resilient and sustainable energy. We are committed to leading the clean energy transition, meeting our customers’ need for more, cleaner power, while keeping bills as low as possible. Because the people we serve depend on us to power their lives. Headquartered in Minneapolis, we work every day to generate and distribute electricity and gas to customers across eight states: Minnesota, Colorado, Wisconsin, Michigan, North Dakota, South Dakota, New Mexico and Texas. For more information, visit xcelenergy.com or follow us on X and Facebook .

Refresh vs. New Content: How to Improve Rankings [July 2026 Update]
summary: Refresh old blog posts vs. write new content: find out which move wins in July 2026 using Search Console signals, backlink equity, and AI Overview
body_text: You're staring at a content backlog, a folder of posts that used to rank and a list of new ideas someone on the team swears will move the needle. The question isn't which list to trust. It's whether you're even looking at the right data. Refreshing old blog posts versus writing new content sounds like a strategy debate, but it's really just a data question. Your existing pages are already telling you the answer. My goal: you walk away knowing exactly when to refresh, when to write new, and how to build a system so you're never guessing. TLDR: Refresh when a page holds backlinks and ranks in positions 4 to 20. Write new only when there's zero existing coverage. HubSpot found 76% of blog views and 92% of leads came from existing posts, and refreshes drove a 106% traffic increase. Never change the URL. The slug carries your backlink equity. Change it and you reset authority to zero. AI Overviews appear on 13.14% of queries and cut click-through from 15% to 8%. A rewrite alone won't fix that. You have to restructure for citation. Maintouch watches your library, flags pages indexed 90+ days with declining impressions, and runs the refresh autonomously across any CMS collection. Why Content Decay Is a Ranking Problem Content decay is the slow erosion of traffic on a page that used to perform. It doesn't announce itself. A post pulls steady traffic for a year, then loses a position or two. Clicks thin out. By the time you notice, it's off page one and you're not entirely sure when it happened. The mechanics aren't mysterious. Competitors publish fresher answers. Intent changes. Google reads your unchanged timestamp as a staleness signal and starts testing other pages. Left alone, that process compounds, one lost position becomes five, five becomes irrelevance. The good news: content decay is predictable, which means it's stoppable. The bad news is most people catch it late. The SEO Case for Refreshing Old Posts A refresh starts from a position new content can't touch. The page already has backlinks, months of index history, and whatever trust it earned while ranking. A new URL starts from zero: no history, no equity, no signal that Google should trust it over the fifteen other tabs the searcher opened. That head start is why refreshes pay off faster. You're strengthening a page Google already knows, not asking it to gamble on something it's never crawled. HubSpot found 76% of blog views and 92% of blog leads came from existing posts. Refreshing older content drove a 106% traffic increase . The archive is the asset, and most teams just aren't working it. Signals That Tell You a Post Needs a Refresh Open Google Search Console, filter to the last 16 months, and look for these patterns. Clicks falling while impressions hold steady. You still rank, but a SERP feature or a competitor's sharper title is stealing the click. Rewrite the meta and intro first. Impressions and clicks both dropping. That's the clearest sign of decay: Google is showing the page less often and fewer people are clicking when it does appear. Position slipping from the top 3 down into the 4 to 15 range. That window is where a refresh recovers the most ground, and where programmatic SEO tools help you act at scale. Stale stats, dead outbound links, or old product references. Readers notice and bounce. The SERP shifted to listicles, tools, or how-tos, and your post is still a wall of prose. Intent moved without you. When to Refresh Instead of Write New Content Default to a refresh when three conditions line up: the page holds backlinks, has ranking history, and sits in positions 4 to 20 for a keyword you still want. Those pages carry equity a fresh URL would spend six months building. The bigger trap is cannibalization. Publish a second post on a topic you already rank for, and you split authority across two URLs. Google has to pick, and it often picks wrong: the newer page, the shorter page, whatever it decides is the better answer that week. One strong page almost always beats two mediocre ones. Check Search Console before you greenlight any new post. If you're already indexed for that query, consolidate. When Writing New Content Is the Right Move A refresh only works when there's something worth refreshing. Three situations call for a new post instead. You have no existing coverage. If the keyword lives nowhere on your site, there's no equity to build on. Write it new. Intent has moved too far. When the SERP now rewards a format your old post can't become without gutting it entirely, start clean. You'd spend more time retrofitting than building. The old post is thin or off-brand. If salvaging it takes longer than writing fresh, or risks producing AI slop dressed up as a refresh, don't force it. Quick Reference: Refresh vs. Write New vs. Merge vs. Retire Action When to use it Key signal Refresh Page holds backlinks, ranking history, sits in positions 4 to 20 Impressions dropping, position slipping, stale stats Write New No existing coverage for the keyword or topic Zero index history; intent can't be served by an existing URL Merge Two thin posts competing for the same query cluster Split impressions across two URLs, both underperforming Redirect Old post has backlinks but no path to relevance Backlinks exist; content is too far off-topic to salvage Retire Thin, off-topic, or duplicate pages pulling no traffic Zero clicks, no backlinks, hurts overall site quality When to Merge, Redirect, or Retire Content Refreshing assumes there's one page worth saving. Sometimes the right move is different. Merge Two thin posts fighting over the same query cluster should become one. Fold the stronger content into the better-ranking URL, 301 the weaker one to it, and pull those split impressions into a single page that can actually compete. Redirect When an old post has backlinks but no clear path back to relevance, 301 it to the most authoritative page you have on the same topic. The equity moves. The dead weight goes. Retire Thin, off-topic, or duplicate pages with zero traffic aren't neutral; they drag down overall site quality. Noindex them or return a 404. Google reads a leaner archive as a more credible one. How to Refresh a Blog Post for SEO Work through these in order. Skipping steps is how you ship a longer version of the same decaying page: same problems, more words. Pull fresh keyword data. Open Search Console, sort by impressions, find queries the page ranks for but doesn't fully answer. Rewrite the headline and meta description to match current intent. Swap stale stats for current data. Cite the source and year. Fix broken links. Restructure for readability with subheadings and lists. Add internal links using the target's primary keyword as anchor. Add formats AI engines pull from: FAQ block, comparison table, checklist. Apply schema markup for AI search to help engines parse them. Update the publish date. Ship it, then request reindexing. Never Change the URL During a Refresh The URL is the asset. It carries the backlinks, the index history, and every bit of ranking authority the page has accumulated, including signals that matter for answer engine optimization . Change the slug and you reset all of it to zero. Overhaul the title. Rewrite the body. Change the angle entirely if you need to. Just keep the URL exactly as it is. The only acceptable exception is a 301 redirect, and only when a new page completely replaces the old one. Even then, a 301 passes most of the equity, not all. Some authority leaks in the handoff. Move a URL only when you genuinely have no choice. How to Measure Success After a Refresh A refresh isn't done when you hit publish. Give it 4 to 8 weeks before drawing conclusions, and watch these four signals. Impressions and average position in Search Console. Movement here confirms Google has re-crawled and re-assessed the page. Organic clicks and CTR. If CTR is rising at a steady position, your new title and meta are working. Engagement rate in GA4. The earliest signal that the rewrite actually reads better to real humans and bots alike. Featured snippet and AI Overview presence. Gaining or losing the box often moves more traffic than a position change. How AI Search Changes the Refresh vs. New Content Equation Freshness now does double work. A page updated recently gets cited more often by AI engines. Stale timestamps get filtered before content quality is even checked. The harder problem is structural. If traffic is dropping on an informational post, the first thing to check is whether an AI Overview is absorbing the click before anyone reaches your result. AI Overviews appeared on 13.14% of all queries (as of mid-2025, coverage is likely higher by 2026), and click-through drops to 8% when they're present versus 15% when they're not. A rewrite alone won't fix that. You have to restructure for citation: passage-level answers, schema markup, formats that get pulled into the box instead of getting skipped over. Building a Systematic Refresh Cadence A one-off refresh recovers one page. A cadence keeps the whole library from decaying. Let Search Console run the trigger. When a page shows declining impressions or a slipping position across two or more consecutive months, it goes on the list. Set review frequency by topic volatility. Fast-moving subjects like AI or finance get a pass every six months, that's where LLM visibility and AI search rankings shift fastest. Stable evergreen pages, once a year. For a large library, work in this order: Your top 20 pages by traffic. Protect what earns most first. Pages ranking between positions 4 and 20, where the refresh ROI is highest. A rolling backlog, each candidate scored by traffic impact against effort. Clear the high-impact, low-effort ones first and build from there. Run it monthly, and automatic content refreshes stop being a quarterly fire drill. How Maintouch Automates the Refresh vs. New Content Decision Everything above is a manual audit. I built Maintouch to run it for you. The software watches your library and flags any page that's been indexed 90 or more days with declining impressions. No spreadsheet. No monthly scramble through Search Console. Once flagged, background agents run the refresh: updating copy, rewriting metadata, adding internal links from your ranking data (up to 15 per page, anchored to top primary keywords), regenerating schema, and requesting indexing on publish. It runs across any CMS collection, so landing pages and product pages get the same treatment as blog posts. No monthly calendar invite. No project manager keeping score. Final Thoughts on Refreshing Old Blog Posts vs. Writing New Content Refreshing beats writing new content more often than most teams expect. The call gets easier once you know which signals to look for in Search Console. A page that already ranks, even poorly, has a head start that a new URL won't catch up to for months. Protect what you've built before you add to it. I've watched a lot of teams skip the refresh work because it feels less exciting than publishing something new. The posts that come back from the dead always make them regret it. If you want to see how Maintouch handles this automatically (watching your library, flagging decay, running the refresh), shoot me a message at [email protected] and I'll walk you through it. FAQ Should you refresh old blog posts or write new content when you're trying to recover lost rankings? Default to a refresh when the page holds backlinks, ranking history, and sits in positions 4 to 20 for a keyword you still want. That equity takes months to rebuild on a new URL. Why throw it away? Write new content only when there's no existing coverage, when the old URL can't be restructured to match current intent, or when the post is so thin that salvaging it genuinely takes longer than starting clean. How do I know which pages to refresh first using Google Search Console? Sort by impressions over the last 16 months. Look for clicks falling while impressions hold steady, both dropping together, positions sliding from the top 3 into the 4 to 15 range, or stale stats and broken links that make readers bounce. Pages sitting in that 4 to 20 position window recover the most traffic from a refresh. Those are your highest-priority candidates. What's the fastest way to refresh a blog post for both Google rankings and AI citations in 2026? Do it in one pass: rewrite the headline and meta, swap in current data with sources, restructure the body into passage-level answers, add an FAQ block and comparison table, regenerate schema, update internal links anchored to your top keywords, then request reindexing the moment you publish. That full pass is what earns both ranking recovery and citation eligibility. Skip the schema step and your page can get filtered out of the AI retrieval set before content quality is even considered. When should I merge two blog posts instead of refreshing them separately? Merge when two thin posts are competing for the same query cluster: fold the stronger content into the better-ranking URL, then 301 the weaker one to it. Splitting impressions across two pages weakens both; a single consolidated page pulls that authority into one URL that can actually win. Can Maintouch automate the refresh vs. new content decision for an existing blog library? Yes. Maintouch watches your library and flags any page indexed 90 or more days with declining impressions, then background agents run the refresh automatically: updating copy, metadata, internal links (up to 15 per page anchored to top primary keywords), schema, and indexing requests on publish. This runs across any CMS collection, so product pages and landing pages get the same treatment as blog posts, without a manual audit or spreadsheet. How long does it take to see results after refreshing a blog post? Give it 4 to 8 weeks before drawing conclusions. The first signal you'll see is movement in impressions and average position in Search Console, confirming Google has re-crawled and re-assessed the page. Clicks and CTR follow as ranking solidifies. Request reindexing immediately after publishing the refresh so you're not waiting on Googlebot's natural crawl schedule. Does refreshing old content hurt your SEO if you change too much? No, as long as you keep the URL. Overhaul the title, rewrite the body, restructure the post, change the angle entirely. None of that touches your ranking history or backlink equity. The slug is the asset. The only thing that kills authority is changing the URL. What's the difference between a content refresh and just updating a publish date? Google has learned to detect timestamp manipulation, and it largely ignores it. A real refresh means updating stats with current sources, restructuring for readability, fixing broken links, rewriting the headline and meta, and adding formats (FAQ blocks, comparison tables) that serve both rankings and AI citation. The timestamp should reflect genuine work. If you can't point to at least five substantive changes, you haven't refreshed the post. How do I decide between consolidating two posts versus refreshing one of them? Check whether both posts are pulling impressions for the same query cluster in Search Console. If you see split impressions across two URLs and both are underperforming, consolidate: fold the stronger content into the better-ranking URL and 301 the weaker one to it. If one post clearly dominates impressions and the other targets a genuinely different intent, refresh them separately. Should I refresh a post that was never ranking well to begin with? Depends on why. If it has backlinks and index history but thin or misaligned content, a refresh can work. The equity is there, it just needs better content on top of it. If it has zero backlinks, no ranking history, and the competition has gotten stronger since you first published, you're better off starting fresh. A poor track record isn't the same as no track record. How does content freshness affect AI search citations beyond Google rankings? AI engines weight recency explicitly, not because they prefer newer ideas, but because freshness signals the information is reliable. Content updated in the last 90 days gets cited far more often than stale pages. When you refresh a post, you buy back into that eligibility window. Stale timestamps get filtered before content quality is even checked. A strong post with an old update date can be completely invisible in AI-generated answers, even if it's sitting on page one of Google.

title: Spott Update - June 2026
summary: Import jobs from the web, new candidate-to-job matching actions, calendar management, expanded automations, Boolean search, and more in Spott's June update.
body_text: Hey there 👋 June was about turning insight into action faster. We made it easier to pull opportunities and candidates into your workflow, added new actions right where you find your matches, brought calendar management into the platform, and gave power users sharper search and automation tools. Grab a coffee. Here is what shipped. ☕️ TL;DR Import jobs from the internet - Pull any publicly visible job straight into Spott from the Browser Extension Candidate-to-job matching actions - Pitch candidates to multiple jobs or bulk present them to clients right from the match results Calendar management - Create, reschedule, and cancel invites from the Calendar, and view your teammates' calendars Automation extensions - New time-based automations, field updates, extra filter conditions, and more background actions Candidate Boolean search - Full AND, OR, and NOT support, with Spott switching into Boolean mode automatically Candidates as Cards - A richer card layout for browsing talent alongside the classic table view Plus: analytics drilldown exports to Excel, nested form values in placement exports, and a new Vente integration Big news Import jobs from the internet You can now import any publicly visible job from the internet directly into Spott using the Browser Extension. When you find a role worth working, pull it in where you found it, no manual recreating required. It's an easy way to bring existing opportunities into your workflow and start sourcing against them right away. Candidate-to-job matching Candidate-to-job matching has been upgraded with new workflow actions, so you can act on a match without leaving the results. Pitch a candidate to multiple jobs at once, or bulk present a shortlist to clients in just a few clicks. That's the AI-native loop we care about: Spott surfaces the right matches, and now you can turn them into real pipeline activity faster instead of clicking through separate steps to do it. Calendar management Calendar management is now better integrated into Spott. You can create, reschedule, and cancel calendar invites directly from the Calendar, and view your teammates' calendars to simplify scheduling. That means booking interviews and coordinating across your team happens in one place, without bouncing between Spott and a separate calendar app. Automation extensions We've expanded our automation capabilities with a new wave of workflow enhancements. This includes support for time-based automations, field updates, additional filter conditions, and more background actions. Together, these improvements enable more powerful hands-off workflows across the platform, so more of the routine work runs itself while you focus on placements. Candidate Boolean search Candidate Search now supports full Boolean queries, including AND, OR, and NOT operators for more precise sourcing. Enter your search using Boolean syntax, and Spott automatically detects and switches into Boolean mode when quotes are used. For power users, that means much greater control over your results without leaving the search bar. Candidates as Cards Candidates can now be viewed in a card layout in addition to the traditional table view. Fewer records are visible at once, but each card provides richer context and key details at a glance, giving you a more visual way to browse and review talent. More improvements this month June also brought a couple of upgrades for teams that live in reporting and placement data. Analytics exports to Excel. You can now export analytics drilldowns directly to Excel for additional analysis and modeling, giving teams more flexibility when working with data in their preferred BI tools. From any Report, hit the dots at the top right to find the 'Export to Excel' option. Placement form exports. Placement exports now include nested form values directly in the Excel output, so you can analyze placement data without manually combining information from multiple sources. The additional fields are available immediately for reporting and BI workflows. Vente integration. Spott now connects with Vente , which scans the web for live hiring signals - open roles with hiring manager contacts - and pushes them straight into Spott. New business development leads land in your workspace automatically, so you can reach out to companies that are actively hiring without leaving Spott. That's a wrap on June As always, keep the feedback coming. It shapes what we build next. If you're not on Spott yet and want to see what an AI-native ATS looks like, book a demo . See you in July. 👋

title: Pairing Framed Art with Houseplants
summary: Elevate your space by pairing lush houseplants with beautiful custom frames, a classic combo that can bring life, color and warmth to any room.
body_text: There's something inherently pleasing about bringing nature indoors, especially when paired with art that speaks to your soul. Combining houseplants with framed photos and artwork is a timeless decor tip that can transform any space into a sanctuary of warmth, color, and creativity. Continue reading below as we cover some of the benefits of this pairing and a few tips for harmoniously blending greenery with art! The Benefits of Pairing Art and Plants Visual Balance - The contrast between the structured lines of a framed piece and the organic forms of plants creates a visually pleasing balance in your space, making it more inviting. Original artwork framed with a 1" black profile and 2.5" of matting Mood Boost - Studies have uncovered evidence that houseplants can reduce stress and increase feelings of well-being. Surrounding yourself with art and meaningful framed photos has shown to have similar benefits. The combination can create the feeling of a peaceful oasis in your home. This applies equally to your workspace, where a feeling of calm and order can work wonders for your productivity. Gallery style white profile and mat, framed at home by @ssma11z with our DIY framing kits Air Quality - Plants are nature's air purifiers, removing indoor pollutants and producing fresh oxygen. Surrounded by art and greenery, you're not only beautifying your space but also making it healthier! Custom framed wedding photo in 3/4" walnut, printed on archival matte fine art paper Versatility - Both plants and art come in a vast range of sizes, colors, and styles. This means endless combinations and opportunities to refresh the look of your interiors. Tips & Tricks for a Harmonious Pairing Coordinate Colors - Choose plants that complement the color palette of your artwork. For instance, a framed piece with rich orange tones or a sunset might pop next to a pot or foliage with a complementary accent color. Play with Heights - Use plant stands, books or hanging pots to vary the heights of your plants, creating a multi-dimensional look when combined with wall-hung art. Framed artwork featuring prints by Invisible Creature Choose the Right Spot - Ensure the spot you choose for your plant gets the right amount of sunlight. Similarly, keep valuable artwork out of direct sunlight to prevent fading. On everything we frame, we offer the option of UV-protective glaze to protect your artwork and photos from sun damage. Theme It Up - If you have an artwork of a coastal scene, pairing it with plants like palm or ferns can amplify the beachy vibe. Similarly, a desert landscape goes well with cacti or succulents. Did you know that we specialize in framing oversize prints and artwork ? Scale Matters - Don’t pair a small framed photo with an oversized plant or vice-versa. Ensure that both the art and the plant are to scale with each other and the space. Framed photo in our Academie Gold profile, part of the Classic Collection of frame colors If you are filling up an entire gallery wall of framed photos , make sure your plants do not get overwhelmed. When the scale is right, plants and framed pieces can complement and elevate each other, creating focal points in a room. A mismatched scale can lead to missed opportunities for creating these visually appealing combinations. Over to you! Art and houseplants are a match made in decor heaven. They bring together the best of human creativity and nature's beauty. So, if you're looking to breathe life into your home, this pairing is the way to go. Get creative, experiment with combinations, and watch your space transform! If you need to start with the frames, we have numerous ways to take your best pictures and turn them into beautifully framed wall art, including our collage picture frames which can combine multiple images to tell a story with photos . The Offset (17" x 17" outer dimensions) - one of the many curated collage frame layouts we offer Don't forget to water your plants, and that a little maintenance on your wall decor can go a long way in helping it last as long as possible. Read our top tips and tricks for that in How to Take Care of your Picture Frames . Happy framing!

title: HRA Calculation & Tax Exemption: Rules, Formula & Examples for HR Teams
summary: What is HRA (House Rent Allowance)? House Rent Allowance (HRA) is a salary component paid by employers to employees to cover the cost of rented accommodation. It is one of the most common components in the salary structure of Indian companies, appearing in the CTC breakdown of nearly every salaried professional who receives a structured […]
body_text: Insights & Resources HRA Calculation & Tax Exemption: Rules, Formula & Examples for HR Teams July 15, 2026 Shashank Yadav No comments yet What is HRA (House Rent Allowance)? House Rent Allowance (HRA) is a salary component paid by employers to employees to cover the cost of rented accommodation. It is one of the most common components in the salary structure of Indian companies, appearing in the CTC breakdown of nearly every salaried professional who receives a structured pay package. HRA exemption under Section 10(13A) of the Income Tax Act, 1961 , allows salaried individuals to reduce their taxable income by claiming a deduction on the rent they pay. This exemption is not automatic — it must be calculated using a specific formula and supported by proper documentation submitted to the employer. According to payroll data aggregated from major Indian HR platforms, over 60% of salaried individuals in metro cities claim HRA exemption every financial year, making it one of the most widely used tax-saving provisions in the country. For employees in cities like Mumbai, Bengaluru, and Delhi — where rental costs can consume 30% to 50% of take-home pay — the HRA exemption provides significant financial relief. For HR teams and payroll administrators, understanding HRA is not optional. Incorrect HRA calculations can lead to TDS short-deduction notices from the Income Tax Department, employee grievances during tax filing season, and compliance issues during payroll audits. Getting HRA right requires understanding the formula, the documentation rules, the metro city classifications, and the interplay between the old and new tax regimes. HRA is typically structured as 40% to 50% of Basic Pay in most Indian companies, though the exact percentage varies by employer policy and location. While HRA is fully taxable by default, the exemption provisions allow employees to claim partial or full relief — provided they actually pay rent and submit the required proofs. Key Point for HR Teams HRA exemption must be calculated month-wise (not annually) for TDS purposes. If an employee’s rent, salary, or city changes mid-year, the calculation must be updated for each relevant month. SalaryBox automates this entire process, recalculating dynamically when any parameter changes. HRA Exemption Formula Under Section 10(13A) The HRA exemption under Section 10(13A) of the Income Tax Act is calculated as the lowest of three prescribed amounts . This three-way comparison ensures that the tax benefit is proportional to the employee’s actual rent burden and is not inflated beyond what they actually spend on housing. HRA Exemption = LOWEST of the following three: 1. Actual HRA received from the employer 2. 50% of salary (metro cities) OR 40% of salary (non-metro cities) 3. Actual rent paid MINUS 10% of salary This formula means the exemption can never exceed the HRA you receive, can never exceed a threshold linked to your salary and city, and is always reduced by 10% of your salary (representing the portion you are expected to bear regardless of your rent). Definition of ‘Salary’ for HRA Calculation For the purpose of HRA exemption, ‘Salary’ is defined narrowly and includes only the following components: • Basic Pay • Dearness Allowance (DA) — only if it forms part of retirement benefits (i.e., if DA is considered for PF/gratuity calculation) • Commission — only if it is a fixed percentage of turnover (not discretionary bonuses) Important: Other allowances such as Special Allowance, Conveyance Allowance, Medical Allowance, Performance Bonuses, and Overtime Pay are NOT included in the salary definition for HRA calculation. This is one of the most common errors HR teams make when computing HRA exemption. Including these components inflates the salary figure, which distorts both Option 2 and the 10% deduction in Option 3, leading to incorrect exemption amounts. New Metro Cities for HRA from April 2026 Major Update — Effective April 1, 2026 From FY 2026-27, Rule 279 of the Income Tax Rules 2026 expands the list of metro cities for HRA purposes from 4 to 8. Employees in the newly classified metro cities — Bengaluru, Pune, Hyderabad, and Ahmedabad — now qualify for the higher 50% of salary benchmark instead of the previous 40%. Metro vs Non-Metro Classification (FY 2026-27 Onwards) City Classification HRA % of Salary Status Mumbai Metro 50% Existing (unchanged) Delhi (NCR) Metro 50% Existing (unchanged) Kolkata Metro 50% Existing (unchanged) Chennai Metro 50% Existing (unchanged) Bengaluru Metro 50% NEW from April 2026 Pune Metro 50% NEW from April 2026 Hyderabad Metro 50% NEW from April 2026 Ahmedabad Metro 50% NEW from April 2026 All other cities Non-Metro 40% Unchanged Why This Change Matters: India’s IT and business landscape has evolved significantly since the original four-city metro list was established. Bengaluru, Pune, Hyderabad, and Ahmedabad have become major employment hubs with rental costs approaching those of the traditional metros. The expansion recognizes this reality and provides fairer tax treatment to employees in these cities. Impact for HR Teams: If you have employees based in any of the four newly added metro cities, their HRA exemption calculation changes from April 2026. Payroll systems must be updated to apply the 50% rate instead of 40% for these locations. SalaryBox has already updated its HRA engine to incorporate the expanded metro city list automatically. For example, an employee in Bengaluru with a basic salary of Rs 50,000 previously qualified for 40% (Rs 20,000) under Option 2, but now qualifies for 50% (Rs 25,000). Depending on which option ends up being the lowest, this can result in additional annual tax savings of Rs 15,000 to Rs 30,000 based on the employee’s tax bracket. Step-by-Step HRA Calculation with Worked Examples Below are three detailed examples covering the most common scenarios HR teams encounter. Each example follows the standard three-step comparison method under Section 10(13A). Example 1: Metro City Employee (Bengaluru — Newly Classified Metro) Employee Profile: Rahul is a software developer based in Bengaluru. He lives in a rented apartment in Whitefield. Component Monthly Amount (Rs) Basic Pay 40,000 Dearness Allowance (DA) 5,000 HRA Received from Employer 20,000 Actual Rent Paid to Landlord 18,000 Step-by-Step Calculation: Step 1: Determine Salary for HRA purposes Salary = Basic Pay + DA = Rs 40,000 + Rs 5,000 = Rs 45,000 Step 2: Calculate all three options Criterion Formula Amount (Rs) Option 1 Actual HRA received 20,000 Option 2 50% of Salary (Bengaluru is metro from Apr 2026) 22,500 Option 3 Rent paid – 10% of Salary = 18,000 – 4,500 13,500 Step 3: Select the lowest Result Exempt HRA = Rs 13,500/month (lowest of the three) Taxable HRA = Rs 20,000 – Rs 13,500 = Rs 6,500/month Annual tax-exempt HRA = Rs 13,500 x 12 = Rs 1,62,000 Annual taxable HRA = Rs 6,500 x 12 = Rs 78,000 Note: Before April 2026, Bengaluru was non-metro. Option 2 would have been 40% of Rs 45,000 = Rs 18,000. In this specific case the exemption remains Rs 13,500 (Option 3 is still lowest), but for employees where Option 2 was the binding constraint, the reclassification delivers tangible savings. Example 2: Non-Metro City Employee (Jaipur) Employee Profile: Priya works as an HR manager at a manufacturing firm in Jaipur. She does not receive DA as part of her salary. Component Monthly Amount (Rs) Basic Pay 30,000 HRA Received from Employer 12,000 Actual Rent Paid 10,000 Calculation: Salary = Basic = Rs 30,000 (no DA applicable) Criterion Formula Amount (Rs) Option 1 Actual HRA received 12,000 Option 2 40% of Salary (Jaipur is non-metro) 12,000 Option 3 Rent paid – 10% of Salary = 10,000 – 3,000 7,000 Result Exempt HRA = Rs 7,000/month (lowest) Taxable HRA = Rs 12,000 – Rs 7,000 = Rs 5,000/month Annual tax-exempt HRA = Rs 7,000 x 12 = Rs 84,000 In this case, Option 3 is significantly lower than the other two options. This is common when the rent-to-salary ratio is moderate. To maximize exemption, the employee would need to either pay higher rent or have a higher salary component dedicated to HRA. Example 3: Employee Who Does Not Pay Rent If an employee owns their home, lives with family without paying rent, or occupies employer-provided accommodation, the entire HRA received is fully taxable . No exemption is available under Section 10(13A) because the fundamental condition — actually paying rent for residential accommodation — is not met. When rent paid is zero, Option 3 (Rent paid minus 10% of salary) becomes negative , and the lowest of the three options is therefore zero or negative, meaning the exempt amount is nil. For instance, if an employee receives Rs 15,000 as HRA but pays no rent, the entire Rs 15,000 per month (Rs 1,80,000 annually) is added to taxable income. There is no way to claim partial exemption when no rent is paid. HR Tip Even when an employee does not claim HRA exemption, the HRA component must still appear in the salary structure and on the payslip. It is simply added to taxable income in full. Do not remove HRA from the payslip — only the exemption portion changes. The gross HRA figure remains the same regardless of whether exemption is claimed. Documentation Requirements for HRA Claim (Updated 2026) The Income Tax Department requires specific documentation to validate HRA exemption claims. Under the revised rules effective from FY 2026-27, documentation standards have been tightened, and new disclosure requirements have been introduced. Below is a comprehensive breakdown of what employees must submit and what HR teams must verify. 1. Rent Receipts Monthly rent receipts signed by the landlord are the primary proof of rent payment. Each receipt should include: landlord’s full name, landlord’s address, tenant’s (employee’s) name, rental property address, rent amount, payment period, date of receipt, and landlord’s signature. For receipts exceeding Rs 5,000 , a revenue stamp must be affixed. Many organizations collect rent receipts quarterly — in April, July, October, and January — to maintain an ongoing compliance trail. 2. Rent Agreement A registered or notarized rental agreement is strongly recommended, though not always legally mandated. A written agreement serves as the primary evidence during tax scrutiny or assessment proceedings. The agreement should clearly specify the monthly rent amount, security deposit, lease duration, renewal terms, and complete details of both the landlord and the tenant. For rent agreements with a duration exceeding 11 months, registration with the local sub-registrar is advisable. 3. Landlord PAN Providing the landlord’s PAN (Permanent Account Number) is mandatory when annual rent exceeds Rs 1,00,000 (i.e., monthly rent above approximately Rs 8,333). The employee must obtain the landlord’s PAN and submit it to the employer as part of the HRA declaration process. If the landlord does not possess a PAN, the employee must obtain and submit a written declaration from the landlord containing their full name, complete address, and an explicit statement confirming that they do not have a PAN. This declaration must be submitted along with Form 124. 4. Form 124 (Replaces Form 12BB) Form 124 is the updated investment and expenditure declaration form that employees submit to their employer at the beginning of each financial year. Effective from FY 2026-27, Form 124 replaces the erstwhile Form 12BB. For HRA claims, Form 124 includes a new mandatory field: relationship with landlord . The complete HRA section of Form 124 must contain: • Estimated annual HRA claim amount • Landlord’s full legal name and complete postal address • Landlord’s PAN (or a signed declaration of PAN non-availability) • Relationship with landlord (new field — e.g., unrelated third party, parent, sibling, relative) • Period of tenancy covered by the claim • Monthly rent amount and total rent for the financial year 5. Payment Mode and Proof Rent payments through bank transfer, UPI, or cheque are strongly preferred as they create an automatic, verifiable payment trail. Bank statements showing regular monthly transfers to the landlord serve as robust supporting evidence. Cash payments, while not explicitly prohibited by the Income Tax Act, attract significantly higher scrutiny from the Income Tax Department during assessment proceedings. For rent amounts above Rs 50,000 per month, digital payment is practically essential for the claim to withstand examination. Landlord PAN & Form 124 Rules in Detail The landlord PAN requirement is one of the most frequently misunderstood and mishandled aspects of HRA compliance. Let us break down the rules with complete clarity. Annual Rent Paid Landlord PAN Required? Action if Landlord Has No PAN Up to Rs 1,00,000 No — optional but recommended No specific action needed Above Rs 1,00,000 Yes — mandatory per IT rules Written declaration from landlord required Form 124: What HR Teams Must Know Form 124 replaced Form 12BB effective from FY 2026-27 as the standard employee investment and expenditure declaration form. Key differences and compliance points: • New mandatory field requiring disclosure of the landlord-tenant relationship • Digital submission is accepted — e-signed copies are valid • Provisional Form 124 must be submitted by April 30 each year for initial TDS calculation • Final proofs and updated Form 124 must be submitted by January 15 for actual TDS adjustment in February-March • Employer must retain Form 124 and all supporting documents for 7 years from the end of the relevant assessment year • Discrepancies between provisional and final declarations must be reconciled in the last quarter TDS HRA Under Old Tax Regime vs New Tax Regime The choice between the Old and New Tax Regimes is one of the most impactful financial decisions for salaried employees, and HRA exemption availability is a major differentiating factor. HR teams are frequently asked for guidance on this choice, making it essential to understand the comparison clearly. Parameter Old Tax Regime New Tax Regime (Sec 115BAC) HRA Exemption Available under Sec 10(13A) NOT available – HRA fully taxable Standard Deduction Rs 50,000 Rs 75,000 Section 80C Deduction Up to Rs 1,50,000 NOT available Section 80D (Medical Insurance) Available NOT available Home Loan Interest (Sec 24) Up to Rs 2,00,000 NOT available Tax Slab Rates Higher rates, more deductions Lower rates, minimal deductions Best Suited For Employees with rent + investments Employees with few deductions Decision Framework for Employees Choose Old Regime if your total deductions (HRA + 80C + 80D + home loan + NPS + others) exceed approximately Rs 3,75,000 per year. The higher tax rates are more than offset by the deductions. Choose New Regime if your deductions are minimal — for example, if you own your home (no HRA claim), have few investments under 80C, and prefer simplicity with lower tax rates. HR teams should provide employees with a comparative tax calculator to help them make informed decisions. SalaryBox includes a built-in old vs new regime comparison tool that factors in HRA, 80C, 80D, and all other major deductions. Special HRA Scenarios Every HR Team Must Know 1. Paying Rent to Parents An employee can pay rent to their parents and claim HRA exemption . This is a legally valid arrangement confirmed by multiple Income Tax Appellate Tribunal (ITAT) decisions. However, certain conditions must be strictly met for the claim to hold up during scrutiny: • The parent must be the legal owner of the property (ownership documents should be available) • A formal rent agreement must exist between the employee (tenant) and parent (landlord) • Rent must be paid through traceable means — bank transfer or UPI, not cash • The parent must declare the rental income received in their own Income Tax Return (ITR) • Form 124 must disclose the relationship as ‘Parent’ in the new mandatory relationship field Tax planning note: If the parent is a senior citizen in a lower tax bracket — or has income below the basic exemption limit — this arrangement creates a legitimate net tax saving for the family. The employee saves tax through HRA exemption, and the parent’s rental income may fall within their exemption limit or attract a lower tax rate. 2. Joint Rent with Spouse When both spouses are salaried and live in the same rented accommodation, only one spouse can claim HRA for the same property . The claim must be made by the spouse in whose name the rent agreement and rent receipts are issued. Dual claims on the same property will be flagged during automated ITR processing and can trigger scrutiny notices for both individuals. However, if both spouses work in different cities and maintain separate rented accommodations, each can independently claim HRA for their respective rental property. 3. HRA and Home Loan Together Claiming both HRA exemption (Section 10(13A)) and Home Loan interest deduction (Section 24) simultaneously is legally permissible — but only under a specific condition: Dual Benefit: HRA + Home Loan The rented property (for which HRA is claimed) must be in a different city from the owned property (for which home loan deduction is claimed). For example, an employee working in Mumbai who rents an apartment there but owns a home in Lucknow can claim HRA exemption for the Mumbai rental and home loan interest deduction for the Lucknow property — both under the old tax regime. 4. Part-Year Metro, Part-Year Non-Metro If an employee transfers from a metro city to a non-metro city (or vice versa) during the financial year, HRA exemption must be calculated month-wise based on the actual city of residence for each month. The 50% and 40% rates are applied to the respective months, and the annual exemption is the sum of all monthly calculations. For example, if an employee works in Bengaluru (metro, 50%) from April to September and transfers to Jaipur (non-metro, 40%) from October to March, each six-month period uses its respective rate. The employer must track the transfer date and adjust TDS calculations accordingly. 5. Multiple Employers in the Same Year When an employee changes jobs mid-year, each employer calculates HRA exemption independently for their respective employment period. The employee must provide rent details and Form 124 to each employer separately. At the time of filing their Income Tax Return, the employee aggregates the exemptions from both employers and reports the total taxable and exempt HRA. Any discrepancy or over-claim is resolved during ITR assessment. 10 Common HRA Calculation Mistakes to Avoid Based on payroll audits conducted across thousands of Indian SMBs and analysis of common errors flagged by the Income Tax Department, here are the ten most frequent HRA mistakes that lead to incorrect tax deductions, employee grievances, and compliance notices: 1. Using annual salary instead of monthly salary HRA exemption must be computed on a monthly basis. Using annual figures inflates the 10% deduction in Option 3 and produces incorrect exemption amounts. The month-wise calculation is especially critical when salary or rent changes mid-year. 2. Including allowances beyond Basic + DA in salary Only Basic Pay, DA (if part of retirement benefits), and fixed commission are included in the salary definition for HRA. Including Special Allowance, HRA itself, Transport Allowance, or Performance Bonuses inflates the salary figure and produces wrong results. 3. Not recalculating when rent or salary changes mid-year If an employee receives a mid-year increment, changes rental accommodation, or moves to a different city, the HRA exemption must be recalculated from the month of change onwards. Many payroll teams make the mistake of using start-of-year figures for the entire year. 4. Claiming HRA under the new tax regime HRA exemption is NOT available under Section 115BAC (new regime). Employees who opt for the new regime cannot claim any HRA deduction — the entire HRA received is taxable. HR teams must validate regime selection before processing HRA exemptions. 5. Missing landlord PAN for rent above Rs 1 lakh annually Failure to collect and report the landlord’s PAN when annual rent exceeds Rs 1,00,000 can result in the entire HRA exemption being disallowed during assessment. The employer is also liable for not performing due diligence. 6. Not updating metro classification for the four new cities From April 2026, Bengaluru, Pune, Hyderabad, and Ahmedabad are classified as metro cities for HRA. Using the old 40% rate instead of 50% understates the employee’s exemption and results in excess TDS deduction. 7. Calculating HRA for the full year when rent was paid for fewer months If an employee paid rent for only 8 months (e.g., moved to own house mid-year), HRA exemption is available only for those 8 months. The remaining months’ HRA is fully taxable. 8. Not collecting Form 124 on time Provisional declarations should be submitted by April 30 and final proofs by January 15. Late submissions create TDS adjustment complications and may result in excess tax deduction that the employee must claim as refund during ITR filing. 9. Ignoring the landlord relationship disclosure requirement The new Form 124 requires disclosure of the landlord-tenant relationship. Omitting this field can trigger scrutiny, especially when rent is paid to family members like parents or siblings. 10. Allowing HRA claims without rent receipts Even if a rent agreement exists, monthly rent receipts are the primary supporting evidence required. Receipts above Rs 5,000 must have revenue stamps. Claims without receipts are routinely disallowed during assessment.year Related Shashank Yadav Leave a Reply Cancel reply

title: Pine Park Health | Managing Medications as We Age: Tips and Strategies for Older Adults
summary: As we age, our bodies go through a number of changes, and some of these changes result in the need for medication.
body_text: As we age, our bodies go through a number of changes, and some of these changes result in the need for medication. Today, about one-third of older adults living in the US are prescribed 5 or more medications each day. While many medications offer life-saving benefits, taking too many medications (polypharmacy) poses a chance of harmful interactions. Polypharmacy may also cause side effects that can have a negative impact on your quality of life. As primary care providers, our role is to offer personalized care to each individual patient and optimize their medications for their current needs. How Medication Management Can Improve Quality of Life Recently, I reviewed medications on a 95-year-old patient who was taking 20 prescribed medications a day. It was very challenging for her to take all of these medications because some had to be taken on an empty stomach and others only after eating. She felt as if she were chained to her medication cabinet and watched the clock all day long. After careful review, there were many issues identified. One example was a duplication of medication where she was taking the same medication each day and wasn’t aware that one was generic and the other was the same, just under a brand name. By eliminating the brand, we reduced her medication and saved her money. Additionally, she had two medications added to combat the side effects of her ibuprofen, which is not an optimal medication for older adults. By working with her, and the therapy department, we added some gentle exercise and the use of a heating pad to alleviate her low back discomfort and were able to discontinue three medications and improve her overall mobility. The medication management program focuses on what is essential for the each patient's health and current conditions. Providers should monitor all medications, decide if medications are still necessary, and ensure medications do not interfere with What Matters, Mentation, or Mobility. Medication Management Challenges in Senior Living There are unique challenges when it comes to managing medications for older adults, especially in senior living communities. Polypharmacy, confusion, and cost are some of the most significant challenges. Polypharmacy : Older adults are being prescribed many medications, and some of those interactions cause side effects that can alter an older person's quality of life. Polypharmacy is the simultaneous use of multiple medications by one individual to treat one or more conditions, and it can lead to an increased risk of adverse drug reactions, falls, and cognitive impairment. Confusion : Some older adults may be confused about which medications they're supposed to take, when, and for how long. This confusion can be due to cognitive impairment, changes in medication regimens, and the complexity of the medication regimen. Some older adults may also forget to take their medication or take it more frequently than prescribed, leading to side effects and adverse drug reactions. Cost : Medication distribution is an additional expense that can create a barrier for some residents and/or families. Distribution frequency is also often connected to senior living community charges – it's an expense from the pharmacy and a charge for each distribution. This cost can make it challenging to afford medications, and they may have to choose between taking the medications they need and paying for other essential expenses. Managing Medications Successfully There are several steps residents and their families can take to successfully manage their medications. These include: Maintaining an updated written medication list and keeping your primary care provider informed of all medications you’re taking, including over-the-counter medications and supplements. Gathering all of your medications , supplements, and vitamins in one place so you can see everything you’re taking together. Consult with your primary care provider on potential interactions between medications and supplements, vitamins, and even food. Pre-sorting your medications for the week in a pill organizer with enough compartments for all of the medications you need each week and setting up reminders. Know when each medication should be taken and if they should be with or without food. Take note of any new side effects and inform your primary care provider immediately. Common side effects include dry mouth, dizziness, headache, blurred vision, unstable gait, constipation, loss of appetite and more. Set up refill reminders. Check if your pharmacy offers automatic refills and deliveries. Another convenient option is to request 90-day supplies through a mail service pharmacy for long-term medications. When you have concerns or questions about your medications and their side effects, be vocal with your care team. Don’t worry about telling providers if you’re not taking them as prescribed. There are many valid reasons for this and you and your provider can help you move past the difficulties with easy-to- follow solutions. As partners in your healthcare, your provider is there to listen and make sure you are involved in making the best informed healthcare decisions for yourself.

title: Thndr Ranks #1 as Africa’s Fastest-Growing Companies 2026, Becoming the First Egyptian Company to Lead the Statista & Financial Times Ranking
body_text: Cairo, Egypt – May 2026 Thndr, Egypt’s leading retail investment platform, has ranked #1 on the Financial Times Africa’s Fastest-Growing Companies 2026 , becoming the first Egyptian company in the ranking’s five-year history to claim the top spot. Compiled by the Financial Times in partnership with Statista, the ranking identifies Africa’s fastest-growing businesses, evaluated across three metrics: absolute revenue growth, compound annual growth rate (CAGR), and employee growth between 2021 and 2024. Thndr ranked the first, ahead of companies from South Africa, Kenya, Nigeria, and across the continent. Since launch, Thndr has now grown to over 5.5 million downloads, with over 75-80% of users investing for the first time. The company has also maintained its position as Egypt’s #1 retail investing platform for three consecutive years. As one of the first fully digital onboarded investment platforms in Egypt, Thndr is now becoming the primary investment account for everyday individuals, offering stocks, gold, savings products, fixed income, and investment funds directly from their phones through a simplified, education-driven experience. Thndr now accounts for around 18% of EGX equity trading value and 40% of EGX total order volume, processing more than 200,000 trades per day, up from 50,000 a year ago. The platform’s reach extends well beyond Egypt’s major cities, with more than 40% of users based outside Cairo and Alexandria. The average user is around 30 years old, and 12% of users are female. The recognition comes as Thndr continues its regional expansion, following its launch in Abu Dhabi in 2025 as the first remote broker on ADX and its recent plan to expand to Saudi Arabia. At a time when only around 0.5% of Egyptians invest, Thndr’s long-term mission remains focused on making investing more accessible and helping build a more financially empowered generation across the Arab world. About Thndr Thndr is the #1 investment platform in Egypt, home to over 5.5 million users across the Arab region. It offers a simple, fully digital way to save and invest in stocks, mutual funds, gold, and savings products, all in one place. The platform provides seamless access to the Egyptian Exchange (EGX), Abu Dhabi Securities Exchange (ADX), and the US exchanges, enabling users to invest across markets with ease. In the UAE, Thndr is the first and only remote broker licensed by ADX. Thndr’s mission is to democratize investing and make it accessible to every individual across the MENA region.

title: As Opus gets smarter, WOZCODE's edge gets bigger
summary: Same prompts, default Claude Code config. Vanilla 4.7 cost 80% more than vanilla 4.6. WOZCODE stayed roughly flat. Savings widened from −41% to −63%.
body_text: ← Blog Opus 4.6 vs. 4.7 April 28, 2026 · 5 min read As Opus gets smarter, WOZCODE's edge gets bigger Vanilla Opus 4.7 costs 80% more than 4.6 on Claude Code's default settings. With WOZCODE installed, the price only increased 12%. Savings widened from −41% to −63% . The expectation The intuition we kept hearing was: "once Claude is smart enough, why do I need a token-saving plugin?" Smarter model picks better tools, takes fewer detours, writes less filler. WOZCODE's edge should compress over time. It's a reasonable hypothesis. We expected the same thing internally, and treated each Opus release as a stress test for whether the plugin still earned its keep. So when 4.7 dropped this week we re-ran our standard code-editing benchmark on both 4.6 and 4.7, vanilla Claude Code vs Claude Code + WOZCODE. The result Same TypeScript codebase, same prompts, same leave-defaults preset (the default config Anthropic shipped with 4.7), just two variables: model (4.6 / 4.7) and plugin (vanilla / WOZCODE). The prompts cover real refactor work: fix a 500 error, split an oversized service class, add JWT typing, set up Jest, and so on. Here's the four-cell matrix: Model Vanilla Claude Code + WOZCODE WOZCODE savings Opus 4.6 $11.62 $6.88 −40.8% Opus 4.7 $20.92 $7.73 −63.1% And it's faster, too. WOZCODE clears the suite in less wall-clock time on both models, and the gap widens on 4.7 the same way the cost gap does: Model Vanilla Claude Code + WOZCODE Time saved Opus 4.6 28m 31s 24m 43s −13.3% Opus 4.7 35m 2s 26m 21s −24.8% Two things jumped out. Vanilla cost nearly doubled. 4.6 to 4.7 went from $11.62 to $20.92 on the same prompts. Per-turn cost rose from roughly $0.05 on 4.6 to $0.13 on 4.7, a 2.6x jump. That's the tokenizer + xhigh effort change Anthropic flagged in the 4.7 launch announcement, fully visible at the default config most users will run. WOZCODE barely moved. $6.88 on 4.6, $7.73 on 4.7, a 12% increase. The relative gap between vanilla and WOZCODE went from $4.74 to $13.19 per run. Quality stayed within noise across all four cells. WOZCODE savings on 4.6 −41% $6.88 vs $11.62 WOZCODE savings on 4.7 −63% $7.73 vs $20.92 Vanilla 4.6 → 4.7 +80% $11.62 → $20.92 Why a smarter model amplifies WOZCODE WOZCODE replaces a handful of Claude Code's built-in tools (Read, Grep, Glob, Edit, NotebookEdit) with versions designed to do more work per call: Combined search + read. One call discovers files and returns matched content, instead of grep → read → read. Batched edits. One call applies many edits across many files, so you stop paying turn-tax on every individual change. AST-aware truncation. Big TS/JS files come back as signatures during exploration; switch to full content only when you've narrowed down. Live SQL introspection. One Sql tool runs queries against connected databases directly: schema discovery, foreign-key graph, real query results. The vanilla pattern is psql-via-Bash plus several rounds of context-padded output; WOZCODE collapses it to a single call. Fuzzy edit matching. Levenshtein-based matching tolerates indentation and whitespace drift, so edits land on the first try instead of bouncing back with "old_string not found" errors that burn another turn. Every one of these tools rewards a planner that thinks before acting. Batched edits only save turns if the model can plan ten edits at once instead of stumbling into them one at a time. Combined search + read only helps if the model knows what it's looking for before it asks. Subagent delegation only works if the model recognizes which subtasks are deterministic enough to hand off. That's exactly the muscle that gets stronger with each Opus release. 4.7 is meaningfully better than 4.6 at recognizing when a single batched call replaces a sequence of small ones, when a signature view is enough vs when to pull full file bodies, when to dispatch a Haiku subagent vs do it inline. WOZCODE on 4.6 took 128 turns to clear the suite. WOZCODE on 4.7 took 52. Same tools, less than half the round trips. Vanilla Claude Code didn't get that benefit, because the tools it has are turn-by-turn primitives. There's no "plan ten edits" call to plan into. The smarter planner has nothing larger to delegate to, so it just spends more thinking tokens per turn at the new xhigh default. That's where the 80% cost increase comes from: 4.7 isn't doing more turns than 4.6, it's doing denser, more expensive turns. What about the price? Anthropic kept Opus 4.7's per-token price identical to 4.6 ($5/$15 per million in/out), but flagged two reasons real spend goes up: Tokenizer update. The same input may produce more tokens. Effort levels. The model tends to think more on harder problems, producing more output tokens at higher effort. At xhigh effort (the new Claude Code default), Opus 4.7 can cost roughly 20–30% more than Opus 4.6 at max effort. — Anthropic, Opus 4.7 launch announcement Our measured number on vanilla Claude Code at leave-defaults is +80%, well past Anthropic's stated range. Some of that is workload-specific (these prompts trigger a lot of cross-file reasoning, which 4.7 spends more output tokens on), but the direction is clear: at the default config Anthropic shipped, the price hike is real and bigger than the headline number suggests. The absolute dollar gap WOZCODE opens up is now $13.19 per run. Run the suite five times in a workweek and that's $66 saved on this one workload, on one developer. What this means going forward The headline finding isn't really about 4.7. It's about the trajectory. WOZCODE's edge widened by 22 points moving from 4.6 to 4.7. The safe assumption for 4.8, 5.0, and beyond is that the gap keeps widening, not closing. Better planners get more out of better tools. Vanilla Claude Code's tools don't change shape with the model; WOZCODE's do. That asymmetry compounds. If you're on Claude Code's flat plan (Pro / Max / Team), the dollar bill doesn't change but your usage cap fills up faster on 4.7. WOZCODE finishes the same suite in 52 turns vs vanilla's 161, so you burn roughly a third of the budget per task. If you're paying per-token (API or pass-through), upgrading from 4.6 to 4.7 adds about $0.85 per run with WOZCODE installed ($6.88 → $7.73). Without WOZCODE, the same upgrade adds $9.30 per run ($11.62 → $20.92). Installing the plugin and upgrading the model in the same week leaves you ahead on every dimension. Either way: 4.7 is the smartest Opus yet, and you should use it. Just don't pay full price. Cut your Opus 4.7 bill nearly in half Install WOZCODE in under a minute. No code leaves your machine, no config to manage. Install WOZCODE → Benchmark methodology: identical TypeScript codebase, both runs on April 28, 2026. The leave-defaults preset means the runner doesn't override Claude Code's effort or thinking settings, so each model runs with whatever Claude Code ships as its default. For 4.7 that's the new xhigh effort level; for 4.6 it's the prior default. This is what most users will see out of the box. Per-prompt breakdowns and raw run logs available on request.
